title: Elevation Certificates on HomeFlood Policies — Acceptance and Re-Rating Guideline
content:
This underwriting guideline sets how an Elevation Certificate is treated on HomeFlood Private Residential Flood Policies.

**G1 — Acceptance.** An Elevation Certificate is accepted for rating only when all of these hold:
- it is on FEMA Form 086-0-33;
- it is completed and sealed by a licensed land surveyor, engineer or architect;
- its survey date is no more than the tier's maximum certificate age, in years, before the date Tidemark receives it;
- the building has not been altered since the survey.

*Status of G1:* **no longer in force** for a certificate review that re-rates the policy's current term under the current certificate review rule. For every other use of a certificate it continues to apply as written.

**G2 — Elevation difference.** The elevation difference is the certified lowest floor elevation minus the base flood elevation, rounded down to the whole foot. A certificate with no base flood elevation feeds only the openings credit.

**G3 — Re-rating.** Tidemark re-rates the current term with the certificate.

**G4 — Lower premium.** When the re-rated term premium is lower, the certificate is applied (its applied flag set to true) from the date it is received. The reduction is credited as a re-rate (RERATE) credit equal to the fall in the full-term premium, multiplied by the days from the receipt date to the term end and divided by the days from the term start to the term end, rounded to the cent.

*Status of G4:* **no longer in force** as the way the re-rate credit following a certificate review is worked out. Every other re-rate credit is still worked out as G4 states.

**G5 — Premium not lower.** When the re-rated premium is not lower, the certificate is kept on file and applied from the next term start, through the renewal rating.

**G6 — Status.** A certificate is applied mid-term only on a policy whose status is pending effective or active, as shown on the policy record.

*Hypothetical illustrations:*
- **Rounding down.** A certified lowest floor 2.7 feet above the base flood elevation gives a difference of 2 feet. A lowest floor 0.4 feet below it gives -1 foot.
- **G4 arithmetic.** In a 365-day term, a fall of 300.00 in the full-term premium with 73 days left from receipt to term end is 300.00 multiplied by 73 and divided by 365, that is 60.00.

superseded_clauses: An Elevation Certificate is accepted for rating only when it is on FEMA Form 086-0-33, completed and sealed by a licensed land surveyor, engineer or architect, and its survey date is no more than ec_max_age_years before the date Tidemark receives it, with no alteration to the building since the survey.

When the re-rated term premium is lower, the certificate is applied (ec_applied true) from the date it is received and the reduction is credited as a RERATE credit equal to the fall in the full-term premium multiplied by the days from the receipt date to term_end divided by the days from term_start to term_end, rounded to the cent.
